neighbours.label: second-person advice to get someone to help: 'ask / let your child (to) help you'
fire: When you sort the laundry, ask your child to help you match the socks.
As you set the table for dinner, let your son help you count the forks.
While you are baking bread, ask the children to help you measure the flour.
When you change the bulb in the hall, ask your daughter to help you.
If you are planting seeds this weekend, let your child help you dig.
When you pack the bags for the trip, ask your teenager to help you.
As you wash the car on Sunday, let the kids help you rinse it.
When you check the smoke alarm each month, ask your child to help you.
quiet: When you sort the laundry, keep the socks apart from the towels.
As you set the table for dinner, put the forks on the left.
While you are baking bread, keep the flour away from the stove.
When you change the bulb in the hall, switch the power off first.
If you are planting seeds this weekend, water the soil well.
When you pack the bags for the trip, put the heavy things at the bottom.
As you wash the car on Sunday, rinse it from the roof down.
When you check the smoke alarm each month, write the date on a card.

notes: Weak pole (max 7.8). Top examples: 'ask the child to help you', 'ask first', 'carry out a small experiment at home'. Probes: 'ask your child to help you' 0.29, 'let your child help you' 0.32, 'ask first' 0.27, 'experiment at home' 0.42; 'ask a neighbour' 0.04, 'The doctor will ask questions' 0.01 (that context belongs to the - pole).
